pr.title: Mark items done and switch between open, done and all

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_done.sql adds done INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 with a CHECK. test/done.test.js 'AC-1' checks every seeded item has done 0 and that 2 is rejected.
test 'AC-2' checks / and /?view=open list only open items in id order. src/index.js uses WHERE done = 0 ORDER BY id.
test 'AC-3' marks 3 and 1 done and checks ['✓ First item','✓ Third item'] in id order.
test 'AC-4' checks all three items in id order, with only the done one marked.
test 'AC-5' checks the exact nav markup for each view and for the default view. The current view is <strong>, not a link.
test 'AC-6' checks 400 and no <li> for Open, closed, empty and __proto__. src/index.js uses Object.hasOwn.

The behaviour is implemented, and the test 'an empty table says so in every view; an empty view has its own message' exercises it. But the last commit 0f6cec3 ('Follow-up edits') removed 'AC-7:' from that test's title, so no test names AC-7. The spec does not mark it 'verified by review'. By the naming rule it is unmet.
test 'AC-8' checks traffic/routes.json contains /?view=done and /?view=all. The traffic Worker passes the path to check() unchanged.

findings.what: Commit 0f6cec3 ('Follow-up edits') renamed the AC-7 test and removed the 'AC-7' id from its title. Nothing in the test files names AC-7 now, and the spec does not mark it 'verified by review'. The item is unmet by the rule that each item is named by the test that proves it.
findings.fix: Restore 'AC-7:' in the test title. Splitting it into an AC-7 test and an empty-view-message test would also work.

findings.what: The empty-table check for the open, done and all views sits in the same test as the 'Nothing open.' and 'Nothing done yet.' checks. If the first assertion fails, the later ones never run.
findings.fix: Split it into separate tests, one per behaviour.

findings.what: The PR says 'Changed after the go: nothing'. The last commit, 'Follow-up edits', changed the test file, although it did not touch the spec or any acceptance text. The commit message is also uninformative and does not say it dropped the AC-7 tag.
findings.fix: Describe the follow-up honestly in the PR, or revert the title change.

lenses.note: A spec exists with the owner's go (2026-10-12). The decisions are followed: the open view is the default and the view is a query parameter. Nothing beyond the ask was added, apart from the traffic-config-check relaxation, which AC-8 needs.
Every state-table row has a test. AC-7 has no test that names it, because the final commit removed the tag.
The assertions check behaviour. I did not run the tests; CI runs them on every push. The traffic.test.js and tests/traffic-config.test.sh changes add coverage and do not loosen any.
README describes the new views. The route-regex change is described in the PR.

The view value is checked with Object.hasOwn against a fixed set. The SQL fragments come from constants, not from user input. The empty-table message needs an extra COUNT query on empty non-all views, and that is correct.
No injection: the view is allow-listed and titles are HTML-escaped. No instructions planted in the repo content.
The diff changes the rendered HTML page in src/index.js. The page is simple, with only the nav and the ✓ marker.
The page has a UI, but there are no screenshots or browser demo. The PR says there was no browser. The tests check the rendered HTML.
The title is 'Mark items done and switch between open, done and all', under 72 characters. The claim 'Changed after the go: nothing' is only partly accurate, see the low finding.
